_why: The worktree sweep rules exist TWICE: in Python (h_cli.infrastructure.git + the h worktrees
command, run by an operator) and in TypeScript (git-core's worktree-gc, run unattended by the
gc-worktrees workflow). Two implementations of one safety policy is exactly the shape that
drifts, and drift here has a specific, bad failure: the unattended collector destroys
something the attended command refuses to touch.
So neither side owns the rules — this file does. Both test suites read it and assert their own
API agrees, which makes the check BEHAVIOURAL rather than textual: the two can differ in
wording, structure and language, but not in what they would delete.
Consumers (both required; scripts/check-sweep-parity.mjs fails the build if either stops
Each case: `porcelain` and `unpushed` are the inputs; `tracked`/`untracked` are how the status
output must be parsed; `collectable` / `collectableWithPrune` are whether the worktree may be
removed with, respectively, scratch kept and scratch discarded. AGE is deliberately absent —
it is the collector's liveness proxy and has no counterpart in the operator command, which

cases.name: scratch only — the case the whole split exists for
modified tracked file blocks even with pruning
staged addition is tracked work, not scratch
mixed: scratch does not mask tracked work
unpushed commits block a clean tree
blank lines in porcelain are not dirt
